summary: Session WorkGate for write, edit, grep, and find at candidate 50079d17c2, the squash of rust/s05-work-gate. HEAD 519a202b13 contains the candidate. There, from a clean checkout, the Linux preflight passed 33 gates under umask 022, with actionlint and runtime skipped, and the Intel x86_64 macOS native preflight passed 4 gates. Their rust gates ran 2422 and 2378 Cargo tests, with 6 ignored on each. Both hosts ran the slice's ownership_tests, both mutation_shutdown cases, and the schedule-look case; tests/session_job_reap.rs ran on Linux only. A Linux preflight under umask 077 at the same commit failed scripts-unit and rust-package because the unpacked bake-rs had mode 0700; no slice touched that code. On the slice branch, the crate and workspace suites passed on Linux. Cross-target Clippy there failed only on bake-cli's print_mode dead code, which the native process slice fixed. No test ran on Windows or Apple Silicon, and the worker's negative controls kept no logs. This record does not supersede 2026-10-14-persistent-settings-credentials, which covers settings and credential storage APIs, not session work ownership.

oracle.notApplicable: No Pi code was adapted. In Pi v1.3.0 (71023aec1546d6d677a65669c5665c0927ce0dd0), AgentSession.dispose() in packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts is synchronous: it aborts and disconnects but awaits no pending tool work. Awaiting owned work at shutdown is Bake's own rule (AGENTS.md, docs/defensive-patterns.md, durable-execution rule 3), and no TypeScript arm applies.

results.behavior: At HEAD 519a202b13, which contains the candidate, the Linux preflight under umask 022 passed 33 gates in 342 s and skipped actionlint (1.7.12 or later not on PATH) and runtime (no runtime source changed). Its log begins with the commit and the umask, and no git status --short line follows them, so the run started from a clean checkout. Its rust gate (76.3 s) ran cargo fmt --check, Clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, and the build: 2422 Cargo tests passed and 6 were ignored. The Intel macOS native preflight passed its rust (193.7 s), rust-pty, rust-package, and rust-eval gates in 302 s: 2378 Cargo tests passed and 6 were ignored. The Mac trace names commit 519a202b13 without the '+ working tree' marker that a snapshot run prints, and host.txt names the same commit. Preflight counts are gates; rust-gate counts are Cargo tests. Each count is taken from each test binary's or doc-test run's own final result line, so the nested subprocess line in bake-coding-agent's tests/bash.rs is excluded. In both rust.log files, the final lines of mcp.rs, mcp_session.rs, and enforcement.rs lack their ignored field, and stdio.rs's line reads only 'test result: ok.'. Its 20 Linux and 19 macOS passes are counted from its 'running N tests' line and its ok lines, and none of those sections lists an ignored test. Off Windows, windows_job_rundown prints only its skip line.

All 7 tests of tools::definition::ownership_tests passed in both rust gates at HEAD, Linux and Intel macOS, and in the slice head's Linux crate and workspace runs. dropped_mutation_waiter_keeps_work_owned_through_file_cleanup covers run_blocking, the write and edit worker. dropped_shared_permit_waiter_keeps_work_owned_through_file_cleanup covers blocking_under with a share of the call's permit, the grep and find path. Each aborts the waiter while the work holds a file open, shows the gate's close pending until the work is released, and shows the work's write complete when close returns. dropped_blocking_waiter_keeps_work_owned_through_file_cleanup does the same for read and ls. In admit_refuses_a_closing_owner, no owner admits without a permit and a closing gate refuses; a permit taken before the close holds the drain. In owned_write_and_edit_refuse_a_closed_owner_without_an_effect, write and edit refuse a closed owner with 'the session is shut down' in their create_tool_definition and owned_sandbox_file_tools forms. The existing file stays unchanged, and a write to a new nested path creates no directory. native_read_and_ls_refuse_a_closed_owner also passed. grep_and_find_refuse_a_closed_owner keeps the texts 'Failed to run ripgrep: the session is shut down' and 'Failed to run fd: the session is shut down'. That test prints a skip and continues when rg or fd is not on PATH, and Cargo captured its output, so no log shows whether either tool ran. rg and fd are in /usr/bin on the Linux host, observed after the run; the Mac's PATH was not recorded. The slice-branch runs tested 548b3baeed, whose tree differs from the candidate's: develop had gained other commits since the branch point 568a6acfa1. The fixture files are byte-identical at HEAD, the candidate, and 548b3baeed. The two slice-branch logs have no exit line; slice-workspace-tests' exit 0 is from its log ('workspace exit 0'), and slice-crate-tests' exit 0 is from the worker report, consistent with every result line being ok. Counts describe Cargo tests.

Both Unix tests of agent_session::tests::mutation_shutdown passed: on Linux and Intel macOS at HEAD, and on Linux at the slice head. hard_agent_shutdown_keeps_sandboxed_write_owned_until_the_worker_returns and its edit counterpart run a real AgentSession with the faux model, which calls the sandboxed tool built by owned_sandbox_file_tools(.., Some(work)). The sandbox's test seam, seam::on_after_check, holds the worker inside the file's mutation queue after the containment check. After the Agent task's hard shutdown and the prompt's end, the gate's close is still pending. Once the worker is released, session.shutdown() returns and the file is unchanged. The tests are cfg(unix) and are not compiled for Windows.

shutdown_stops_a_background_job_and_waits_for_its_group passed in the Linux rust gate at HEAD and in the slice head's Linux runs. The test process is a child subreaper (PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER). A real session's bash starts a background job that holds a descendant in its group ('sleep 1000 & ...; exec sleep 1000'). AgentSession::shutdown does not return within the 500 ms EARLY window while the killed descendant is an unreaped zombie of the test, and it returns once the test reaps that descendant. The job ends Killed with StopCause::Shutdown, and jobs().start is then refused with StartError::Closed. The file is cfg(target_os = "linux"): the Mac rust gate ran its binary with 0 tests, and Windows compiles nothing of it.

agent_session::schedules::tests::shutdown_waits_for_a_look_and_nothing_is_delivered_after passed on Linux and Intel macOS at HEAD, and on Linux at the slice head. The test clock makes a reminder due, and a look held in the clock, inside the session's I/O permit, keeps the gate's close pending after shutdown begins. Shutdown then returns with the gate closed. No dispatch is written, no reminder is posted, and no request reaches the model. The case has no single-point negative control (see missingEvidence).

At HEAD, cargo clippy --keep-going --locked --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings finished with no warning or error for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and for aarch64-apple-darwin (log line 1 is the commit, last line 'exit 0'). The slice's code and its tests compile and lint for Windows and Apple Silicon. This covers compilation and lints only; nothing ran on either target.

The slice's ownership tests on Windows. ownership_tests compile for Windows, except the Unix-only grep_and_find case. mutation_shutdown (Unix) and session_job_reap (Linux) are not compiled there. On the slice branch at 548b3baeed, cross-target Clippy exited 1 (worker report). The log shows only four dead-code errors for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, in bake-cli's tests/print_mode/schedules.rs (outputs, declared) and tests/print_mode/subagents.rs (two_models, is_child). It shows no error for bake-coding-agent or any other crate on Windows, and a clean aarch64-apple-darwin pass. Those helpers belong to the native process slice, whose cfg fix landed on develop in candidate c2144d52a5, before this candidate; the HEAD run is clean (cross-target-lint).

missingEvidence.what: Owned forms of the public file-tool constructors
missingEvidence.reason: create_write_tool_definition, create_write_tool, write::execute_guarded, create_edit_tool_definition, create_edit_tool, edit::execute_guarded, sandbox_file_tools, and create_sandboxed_write_tool_definition and create_sandboxed_edit_tool_definition stay unowned for embedders. Owning them needs a public signature change. The worker report says only tests call them.

missingEvidence.what: A config_value command's stdout reader thread and backgrounded descendants
missingEvidence.reason: The shell runs inside the gate-owned request task's awaited auth thread and is killed and reaped on cancel or timeout. Its detached stdout reader std::thread and any backgrounded descendants are not owned or awaited.
A timed-out probe is killed and awaited. A probe whose future is dropped is killed by kill_on_drop and reaped by Tokio's orphan reaper, but no drain awaits it.

missingEvidence.what: Escaped descendants, a normal exit's backgrounded processes, and bubblewrap namespace teardown
missingEvidence.reason: Every drain leaves these out, unchanged by this slice. tests/process_reap.rs documents the first two.

missingEvidence.what: Job journal writes under their own permit
missingEvidence.reason: job_journal.rs uses a raw spawn_blocking that the gate-owned job driver awaits, so it is owned only transitively. The driver is never aborted, and no dedicated test covers this.

missingEvidence.what: The session-lifetime audit as tested evidence
missingEvidence.reason: The worker's audit of every session-lifetime spawn site and its owner exists only in its report. It found MCP server tasks, background jobs, and the Wasm plugin keeper already gate-owned, so the candidate drops roadmap row 05's stale claim. The audit itself is not a test.
